news.n_ionian_revolt: Word in the harbour is that the Greek cities of Ionia, led by Miletus, have risen against the Persian king.
news.n_miletus_falls: News has come: the Persians crushed the Ionian fleet off Lade and took Miletus. The city is ruined and its people led away into Asia.
news.n_marathon: They say the Athenians, almost alone, defeated a huge Persian army on the plain of Marathon.
news.n_xerxes_king: News has come that the Persian king Darius has died. His son Xerxes has taken the throne, and Egypt is restless again.
news.n_buddha: Merchants from the East say that in distant India a sage whom his followers called the Buddha, "the Awakened One", has died. No one here knows the date for certain.
news.n_laurion: They say a rich vein of silver was struck in the Laurion mines near Athens, and Themistocles persuaded the Athenians to spend it on a fleet.
news.n_thermopylae: News has come that at Thermopylae the Spartan king Leonidas and a handful of men held back the army of Xerxes for days and died to the last man.
news.n_himera: Sailors from Sicily say Gelon of Syracuse destroyed a great Carthaginian army at Himera, on the very day, people claim, of the Greek victory at Salamis.
news.n_plataea: News has come that the Greeks defeated the Persians at Plataea. The army of Xerxes will not return to Greece.
news.n_confucius: Far to the east, in a land almost unknown here, the teacher Kong Qiu, later called Confucius, has died. His students are writing down his sayings.
news.n_delian_league: They say Athens and the islands of the Aegean have formed a league against Persia, keeping its treasury on sacred Delos.
news.n_cumae: Word in the harbour is that Hiero of Syracuse smashed the Etruscan fleet off Cumae. Etruscan ships no longer rule the coasts of Italy.
news.n_persians_play: They say a tragedy by Aeschylus, "The Persians", has been staged in Athens: the defeat of Xerxes seen through Persian eyes.
news.n_eurymedon: News has come that the Athenian Cimon defeated a Persian fleet and army in a single day at the Eurymedon river in Pamphylia.
news.n_xerxes_killed: Merchants from Asia say King Xerxes of Persia has been murdered in his own palace. His son Artaxerxes now rules.
news.n_diagoras: Travellers back from the Olympic Games report that the boxing was won by Diagoras of Rhodes, a giant whom Pindar has praised in an ode.
news.n_sparta_quake: News has come that a terrible earthquake has ruined Sparta, and the helots have revolted and dug in on Mount Ithome.
news.n_inaros: They say that in Egypt a Libyan named Inaros has rebelled against Persia, and Athens has sent a fleet to help him.
news.n_aeschylus_death: News has come that Aeschylus has died at Gela in Sicily. People say an eagle dropped a tortoise on his head, though who can tell.
news.n_league_treasury: They say Athens has moved the allied treasury from Delos to its own Acropolis. The allies grumble that the league has become an empire.
news.n_jin_partition: Far to the east, in the land of silk, three noble houses have carved up the great state of Jin. An age of endless war is beginning there.
news.n_twelve_tables: Merchants from Italy say the Romans have written their laws on twelve tablets and set them up in the forum.
news.n_thirty_years_peace: News has come that Athens and Sparta have made a peace for thirty years. Few believe it will last that long.
news.n_thurii: They say a new colony, Thurii, has been founded in southern Italy by Greeks from all over Hellas, the historian Herodotus among them.
news.n_samos_revolt: Word in the harbour is that Samos has revolted against Athens and Pericles himself has led the fleet against the island.
news.n_athena_parthenos: They say Athens has dedicated a new temple to Athena, and inside stands her statue by Phidias, made of gold and ivory.
news.n_zeus_olympia: Visitors to Olympia say Phidias has finished his statue of Zeus there: a seated god of gold and ivory so huge he nearly touches the roof.
news.n_meton: They say the Athenian astronomer Meton has proposed a calendar in which the moon and the sun come back into step every nineteen years.
news.n_peloponnesian_war: News has come that war has broken out between Athens and Sparta. People say all of Greece will be drawn in.
news.n_herodotus: They say Herodotus of Halicarnassus has written down the history of the Greek wars with Persia and everything he saw on his travels, from Egypt to Scythia.
news.n_pericles_death: News has come that Pericles, who led Athens for thirty years, has died of the plague.
news.n_pylos: Word in the harbour is unbelievable: on the island of Sphacteria Spartan hoplites have surrendered to the Athenians. Not even the old men remember such a thing.
news.n_clouds: They say Athens has staged Aristophanes' comedy "The Clouds", which mocks the philosopher Socrates. Socrates himself, they say, stood up in the theatre so the audience could compare him with the mask.
news.n_peace_nicias: News has come that Athens and Sparta have made a peace, named after Nicias. Prisoners are to be returned.
news.n_hippocrates: People say that on the island of Kos a physician named Hippocrates teaches that diseases have natural causes and are not sent by the gods.
news.n_alcibiades_olympia: From the Olympic Games comes the story that the Athenian Alcibiades entered seven chariots at once and took first, second and fourth place.
news.n_melos: Grim news has come: the Athenians have taken the island of Melos, which refused to join their league, and dealt harshly with its people.
news.n_sicily_sails: Word in the harbour is that a vast Athenian fleet has sailed for Sicily. Just before it left, someone defaced the statues of Hermes all over the city by night.
news.n_sicily_disaster: Terrible news has come: the Athenian army in Sicily has been destroyed entirely. The prisoners labour in the quarries of Syracuse.
news.n_four_hundred: They say four hundred rich men have seized power in Athens and set aside the assembly. The fleet at Samos refuses to obey them.
news.n_selinus: Sailors report that the Carthaginians have returned to Sicily and destroyed the Greek cities of Selinus and Himera.
news.n_tragedians_die: News has come that Euripides and Sophocles have died within months of each other. People say there is no one left in Athens to write tragedy.
news.n_aegospotami: News has come that the Spartan Lysander has captured the Athenian fleet at Aegospotami almost without a fight. Athens has no ships left.
news.n_athens_surrenders: News has come that Athens has surrendered to Sparta. The Long Walls are being pulled down to the music of flutes.
news.n_egypt_free: They say Egypt has thrown off Persian rule again and has a pharaoh of its own.
news.n_zhou_recognizes: Far to the east, in the land of silk, the high king has recognised three usurpers as rulers. The old order there has collapsed for good.
news.n_cunaxa: News has come that Prince Cyrus marched against his brother, the Persian king, and fell at Cunaxa. Ten thousand Greek mercenaries are fighting their way home through the mountains.
news.n_celts_alps: Merchants from the north say Gallic tribes have crossed the Alps and are settling the valley of the Po.
news.n_socrates: News has come from Athens: the philosopher Socrates has been sentenced to death for impiety and corrupting the young. He drank the hemlock.
news.n_kyniska: From the Olympic Games comes the story that a woman has won the chariot race for the first time: the Spartan princess Kyniska, who owned the team.
news.n_veii: Merchants from Italy say the Romans have taken the rich Etruscan city of Veii after a long siege.
news.n_cnidus: Word in the harbour is that the Athenian Conon, with a Persian fleet, has defeated the Spartans off Cnidus.
news.n_gauls_rome: News has come that the Gauls defeated the Romans at the Allia and sacked Rome. They say only the Capitol held out.
news.n_academy: They say the philosopher Plato has opened a school in the grove of Academus outside Athens, and students come from all over Greece.
news.n_kings_peace: News has come that the Greeks have accepted a peace dictated by the Persian king. The cities of Ionia are handed back to Persia.
news.n_leuctra: News has come that is hard to believe: Epaminondas of Thebes has beaten the Spartans at Leuctra. Invincible Sparta has been defeated.
news.n_mantinea: They say the Thebans beat the Spartans again at Mantinea, but Epaminondas himself fell in the battle.
news.n_philip_king: News has come that young Philip has become king of Macedon. They say he is reshaping the army in a new way.
news.n_artemis_burns: News has come that the temple of Artemis at Ephesus, a wonder of the world, has burned. The arsonist wanted fame, so speaking his name is forbidden. They say a royal son, Alexander, was born in Macedon that same night.
news.n_mausoleum: They say King Mausolus of Halicarnassus has died, and his widow is building him a tomb so beautiful it is already spoken of as a wonder.
news.n_shang_yang: Far to the east, in the land of silk, the state of Qin has moved its capital and, on the advice of the stern minister Shang Yang, imposed harsh and strict laws.
news.n_olynthus: News has come that Philip of Macedon has taken and destroyed Olynthus and sold its people into slavery.
news.n_plato_death: They say the philosopher Plato has died in Athens at a great age.
news.n_persia_egypt: News has come that the Persian king Artaxerxes has conquered Egypt again. Nectanebo, the last native pharaoh, has fled south.
news.n_aristotle_tutor: They say King Philip has invited the philosopher Aristotle to tutor his son Alexander.
news.n_ateas: Merchants from the Black Sea say Philip of Macedon has defeated the Scythian king Ateas, a man over ninety years old.
news.n_chaeronea: News has come that at Chaeronea Philip of Macedon has defeated the combined armies of Athens and Thebes. Greece is in his hands.
news.n_philip_killed: News has come that King Philip was murdered at his daughter's wedding, in the theatre. Twenty-year-old Alexander is king.
news.n_thebes_destroyed: News has come that Alexander has taken rebellious Thebes and razed the city, sparing only the house of the poet Pindar.
news.n_granicus: They say Alexander has crossed into Asia and defeated the Persian satraps at the river Granicus.
news.n_issus: News has come that at Issus Alexander has beaten King Darius himself. The king fled, leaving behind his tent and his family.
news.n_tyre: Word in the harbour is that Alexander besieged island Tyre for seven months and took it by building a causeway across the sea.
news.n_alexandria_founded: They say Alexander has founded a new city in Egypt, by the sea, and named it after himself: Alexandria.
news.n_gaugamela: News has come that at Gaugamela Alexander has finally crushed Darius. Babylon has opened its gates to him.
news.n_persepolis: News has come that the palace of the Persian kings at Persepolis has burned, and Darius has been killed by his own satraps. The Persian empire is no more.
news.n_hydaspes: They say Alexander has reached India and defeated King Porus and his war elephants on the river Hydaspes. But the army has refused to go further.
news.n_pytheas: Sailors say Pytheas of Massalia has returned from the far north, telling of an island called Britain where tin is mined, and of a sea there that thickens like jelly.
news.n_alexander_death: News has come that Alexander has died in Babylon at thirty-two. There is no heir, and his generals are already dividing his empire.
news.n_aristotle_death: They say the philosopher Aristotle and the orator Demosthenes have died in the same year; Demosthenes took poison rather than fall into Macedonian hands.
news.n_caudine_forks: Merchants from Italy say the Samnites trapped a Roman army in the Caudine Forks and made it pass under the yoke.
news.n_chandragupta: Merchants from the East say that in India a warrior named Chandragupta has seized power and is building a vast kingdom.
news.n_via_appia: They say the Roman censor Appius Claudius has begun building a paved road south from Rome to Capua.
news.n_seleucus_babylon: News has come that the general Seleucus has recovered Babylon. Years there are now counted from his return.
news.n_agathocles: Sailors tell an incredible tale: Agathocles of Syracuse, besieged by Carthage, has landed in Africa, burned his ships and marched on Carthage itself.
news.n_zhao_cavalry: Far to the east, in the land of silk, the king of Zhao has ordered his soldiers to wear trousers like the steppe nomads and to fight on horseback.
news.n_epicurus: They say the philosopher Epicurus has bought a garden in Athens and teaches there that happiness lies in peace of mind and that the gods need not be feared.
news.n_ptolemy_king: News has come that Alexander's successors have stopped pretending to be governors: Ptolemy in Egypt, Seleucus in Asia and others have proclaimed themselves kings.
news.n_rhodes_siege: Word in the harbour is that Demetrius, called the Besieger, spent a year assaulting Rhodes with enormous siege engines and went away empty-handed.
news.n_seleucus_india: They say Seleucus has ceded his eastern lands to the Indian king Chandragupta and received five hundred war elephants in return.
news.n_ipsus: News has come that at Ipsus the successor kings defeated old Antigonus the One-Eyed. He fell in battle, and the victors are dividing his lands.
news.n_euclid: They say that in Alexandria the mathematician Euclid has gathered all the knowledge of figures and numbers into one book, the "Elements".
news.n_sentinum: Merchants from Italy say that at Sentinum the Romans defeated the Samnites and Gauls together. Rome is becoming master of Italy.
news.n_library: They say King Ptolemy is collecting every book in the world at Alexandria and keeps scholars at the Museum at royal expense.
news.n_heraclea: News has come that King Pyrrhus of Epirus has landed in Italy and beaten the Romans at Heraclea with his elephants.
news.n_colossus: They say the Rhodians have finished a huge bronze statue of the Sun god, the Colossus, taller than any temple. It was paid for by selling Demetrius' siege engines.
news.n_pharos: Sailors say a lighthouse of unheard-of height has been built on the island of Pharos at Alexandria; its fire can be seen far out to sea.
news.n_asculum: They say Pyrrhus beat the Romans again at Asculum but lost so many men that he said, "One more victory like this and I am finished."
news.n_delphi_gauls: News has come that the Gauls have burst into Greece and reached Delphi itself. They say the god defended his shrine with storm and earthquake.
news.n_qu_yuan: Far to the east, the armies of Qin have taken the capital of Chu. They say the poet Qu Yuan threw himself into a river in grief.
news.n_beneventum: News has come that the Romans have beaten Pyrrhus at Beneventum, and he has sailed away from Italy.
news.n_pyrrhus_death: They say King Pyrrhus was killed in street fighting at Argos when an old woman threw a roof tile. And Tarentum has surrendered to Rome.
news.n_septuagint: They say that in Alexandria learned men have translated the sacred books of the Jews into Greek.
news.n_ashoka_king: Merchants from the East say India is now ruled by Chandragupta's grandson, King Ashoka.
news.n_punic_war_1: News has come that Rome and Carthage have gone to war over Sicily. And in Rome, they say, gladiators fought at a funeral for the first time.
news.n_kalinga: Merchants from India say King Ashoka conquered the land of Kalinga, but, seeing the suffering of the defeated, renounced war and has words of mercy carved on rocks.
news.n_mylae: Word in the harbour is that the Romans, who only just built their first fleet, have beaten the Carthaginians at sea off Mylae.
news.n_changping: Far to the east, in the land of silk, the armies of Qin crushed the state of Zhao in a great battle at Changping. They say hundreds of thousands died.
news.n_zhou_ends: Merchants from the East say the ancient royal house of Zhou has fallen in the land of silk. Its lands have been taken by Qin.
news.n_bactria: They say far-off Bactria has broken away from the Seleucid king: its governor Diodotus now rules on his own.
news.n_parthia: Merchants from Asia say Arsaces, chief of a steppe tribe, has seized Parthia and declared himself king.
news.n_aegates: News has come that the Romans destroyed the Carthaginian fleet off the Aegates Islands. The war is over, and Sicily passes to Rome.
news.n_eratosthenes: They say Eratosthenes, keeper of the Library of Alexandria, has measured the whole Earth by the shadow of a stick, and found it two hundred and fifty thousand stades around.
news.n_livius: They say a play in Latin has been staged in Rome for the first time, translated from the Greek by a former slave, Livius Andronicus.
news.n_hamilcar_spain: Sailors say the Carthaginian general Hamilcar Barca has sailed to Iberia to win its silver mines.
news.n_colossus_falls: News has come that an earthquake has toppled the Colossus of Rhodes. The statue lies broken at the knees.
news.n_telamon: They say a huge Gallic army invaded Italy, but the Romans surrounded and destroyed it at Telamon.
news.n_qin_unifies: Far to the east, in the land of silk, the king of Qin has conquered all the warring states and named himself the First Emperor.
news.n_hannibal_command: Sailors from Iberia say the Carthaginian army has chosen twenty-six-year-old Hannibal, son of Hamilcar, as its commander.
news.n_saguntum: News has come that after an eight-month siege Hannibal has taken Saguntum, an Iberian ally of Rome. There will be war.
news.n_hannibal_alps: News has come that sounds like a fairy tale: Hannibal has crossed the Alps with elephants and come down into Italy.
news.n_raphia: News has come that at Raphia King Ptolemy of Egypt defeated the army of Antiochus. They say native Egyptians fought in his phalanx for the first time.
news.n_cannae: News has come that at Cannae Hannibal surrounded and destroyed a vast Roman army. People say Rome has never suffered such a defeat.
news.n_great_wall: Far to the east, they say, the First Emperor has driven back the northern nomads and ordered the old ramparts joined into one endless wall.
news.n_burning_books: Merchants from the East say the emperor in the land of silk has ordered old books burned, except those on medicine, divination and farming.
news.n_archimedes: News has come that the Romans have taken Syracuse. In the chaos the great Archimedes was killed; they say a soldier found him drawing figures in the sand.
news.n_first_emperor_dies: Far to the east, the First Emperor of the land of silk has died. They say he was buried under a mound together with a whole army made of clay.
news.n_new_carthage: They say young Scipio took New Carthage, the Carthaginians' chief city in Iberia, in a single stroke.
news.n_modu: Far to the northeast, on the steppe, a chief named Modu has taken command of the Xiongnu nomads and is forging them into a fearsome power.
news.n_metaurus: News has come that Hannibal's brother Hasdrubal, marching over the Alps to join him, was defeated and killed on the river Metaurus.
news.n_magna_mater: They say the Romans, on the advice of the Sibylline Books, have brought the sacred stone of the Great Mother of the Gods from Asia Minor.
news.n_zama: News has come that at Zama in Africa Scipio has defeated Hannibal himself. Carthage is suing for peace.
news.n_han_founded: Far to the east, in the land of silk, after years of turmoil a commoner named Liu Bang has taken power and founded a new dynasty, the Han.
news.n_baideng: Merchants from the East say the Xiongnu nomads surrounded the Han emperor himself, and he had to make peace by promising the nomads gifts and a bride from his own family.
news.n_panium: News has come that at Panium King Antiochus defeated Ptolemy's army. Judea and Phoenicia pass under Seleucid rule.
news.n_cynoscephalae: News has come that at Cynoscephalae the Roman legions have broken the Macedonian phalanx of King Philip.
news.n_flamininus: They say that at the Isthmian Games the Roman Flamininus proclaimed the Greeks free. People shouted so loudly that stunned birds, it is said, fell from the sky.
news.n_magnesia: News has come that at Magnesia the Romans defeated Antiochus the Great. He will have to leave Asia Minor.
news.n_bacchanalia: They say the Roman Senate has banned the secret rites of Bacchus throughout Italy, and their followers are being hunted down.
news.n_maurya_ends: Merchants from India say the last king of Ashoka's line has been killed by his own general, and the great kingdom has fallen apart.
news.n_hannibal_death: News has come that Hannibal, in exile in Bithynia, has taken poison rather than be handed to the Romans. They say his conqueror Scipio died in those same years.
news.n_pydna: News has come that at Pydna the Romans defeated King Perseus of Macedon. The Macedonian kingdom is no more.
news.n_popillius: They say that just outside Alexandria a Roman envoy drew a circle in the sand around King Antiochus and demanded his answer before he stepped out. Antiochus withdrew from Egypt.
news.n_maccabees: News has come from Judea: rebels led by Judas Maccabeus have taken Jerusalem and rededicated the Temple.
news.n_carneades: They say Athens has sent philosophers to Rome as envoys. Carneades argued one day that justice exists and the next that it does not, and the Roman elders demanded the Greeks be sent home.
news.n_leonidas_rhodes: From the Olympic Games comes the story that the runner Leonidas of Rhodes has won all three footraces for the fourth Games in a row. No one has ever done this.
news.n_menander: Merchants from the East say a Greek king named Menander rules in India and, they say, loves to debate with Buddhist monks.
news.n_carthage_destroyed: News has come that the Romans have taken and destroyed Carthage. The city that fought Rome for a hundred years is gone.
news.n_corinth: News has come that the Romans have destroyed Corinth and shipped its treasures to Rome. Greece is now under Roman rule.
news.n_parthia_babylon: Merchants from Asia say the Parthian king Mithridates has taken Seleucia and Babylon. Parthia has become a great power.
news.n_han_wudi: Far to the east, in the land of silk, a young emperor has taken the throne, the one later called the Martial Emperor, Wudi.
news.n_viriathus: They say Viriathus, the shepherd who led the Lusitanians against Rome for years, has been killed in Iberia, by his own men, bribed by the Romans.
news.n_zhang_qian_out: Far to the east, they say, the emperor of the land of silk has sent an envoy named Zhang Qian westward to seek allies against the nomads.
news.n_numantia: News has come that after a long siege Scipio Aemilianus has taken Numantia in Iberia. Its people held out to the very end.
news.n_pergamon: They say King Attalus of Pergamon has died and left his entire kingdom to the Roman people.
news.n_hipparchus: People say that on Rhodes the astronomer Hipparchus has compiled a catalogue of hundreds of stars, marking where each one stands in the sky.
news.n_zhang_qian_back: Merchants from the East say the envoy of the land of silk has returned home after thirteen years of wandering, telling of the western lands and their wonderful horses.
news.n_gaius_gracchus: News has come from Rome that the tribune Gaius Gracchus has died in street fighting, as his brother Tiberius did twelve years before.
news.n_mobei: Far to the east, they say, Han generals have defeated the Xiongnu nomads deep in the steppe and driven them beyond the desert.
news.n_noreia: Alarming news has come: unknown peoples from the north, the Cimbri and Teutones, have defeated a Roman army at Noreia.
news.n_nanyue: Merchants from the East say the Han emperor has conquered the southern coastal kingdom of Nanyue.
news.n_chersonesus: Merchants from the Black Sea say King Mithridates of Pontus has sent an army to help Chersonesus against the Scythians and taken the Crimea under his protection.
news.n_arausio: News has come that the Cimbri and Teutones have destroyed two Roman armies at Arausio. They say Rome has not known such fear since Hannibal.
news.n_jugurtha: They say the Numidian king Jugurtha, who led the Romans a merry dance for years, has been handed over to them by his own father-in-law.
news.n_sicily_slaves: Sailors say the slaves of Sicily have risen again and proclaimed a king of their own.
news.n_aquae_sextiae: News has come that Marius has destroyed the Teutones at Aquae Sextiae.
news.n_vercellae: News has come that at Vercellae Marius has wiped out the Cimbri. The danger from the north is over.
news.n_ferghana: Far to the east, they say, a Han army crossed the deserts to distant Ferghana and brought back its "heavenly horses".
news.n_tigranes: Merchants from the east say Tigranes has become king of Armenia, a man who dreams, they say, of a great empire.
news.n_social_war: News has come that Rome's allies in Italy have revolted, demanding Roman citizenship. Italians are at war with Rome.
news.n_sima_qian: Far to the east, they say, the court historian Sima Qian has finished a vast history of his land from its earliest kings.
news.n_asian_vespers: Terrible news has come: on a secret order from King Mithridates, thousands of Romans and Italians were killed in the cities of Asia on a single day.
news.n_sulla_athens: News has come that Sulla has taken Athens, which sided with Mithridates. The groves of the Academy were cut down for siege engines.
news.n_sulla_dictator: News has come that Sulla has taken Rome and become dictator. Lists of men declared outlaws are posted in the Forum.
news.n_spartacus: News has come that in Italy gladiators who escaped their school, led by Spartacus, have raised a huge army of slaves.
news.n_pirates: Word in the harbour is that Pompey has swept the whole Mediterranean clear of pirates in three months. Ships sail without fear again.
news.n_syria_province: News has come that Pompey has abolished the Seleucid kingdom. Syria is now a Roman province.
news.n_jerusalem_pompey: News has come that Pompey has taken Jerusalem. Judea is now subject to Rome.
news.n_mithridates_death: Merchants from the Black Sea say King Mithridates, who fought Rome for thirty years, took his own life when his own son betrayed him.
news.n_triumvirate: They say three men in Rome, Pompey, Crassus and Caesar, have secretly agreed to share power among themselves.
news.n_gallic_war: News has come that the proconsul Julius Caesar has begun a war in Gaul.
news.n_caesar_britain: They say Caesar has built a bridge across the Rhine and then crossed the Ocean and landed in Britain, at the edge of the world.
news.n_carrhae: News has come that at Carrhae the Parthians destroyed the army of Crassus, and Crassus himself was killed. The Roman eagles are in Parthian hands.
news.n_alesia: News has come that at Alesia Caesar besieged the Gallic chief Vercingetorix and forced him to surrender. Gaul is conquered.
news.n_huhanye: Far to the east, they say, one of the Xiongnu chiefs has come in person to the Han emperor's court and acknowledged himself his vassal.
news.n_rubicon: News has come that Caesar has crossed the Rubicon with his army and is marching on Rome. Pompey and the Senate have fled. Civil war has begun.
news.n_pompey_death: News has come that Caesar has defeated Pompey at Pharsalus. Pompey fled to Egypt and was killed there as soon as he stepped ashore.
news.n_library_fire: They say many books burned during the fighting in Alexandria. Exactly how many is still argued over.
news.n_julian_calendar: They say Caesar, advised by an Alexandrian astronomer, has introduced a new calendar: 365 days a year, with an extra day every fourth year. This year itself has been stretched to 445 days.
news.n_thapsus: News has come that at Thapsus in Africa Caesar has crushed the last Pompeians. Cato took his own life at Utica.
news.n_caesar_killed: News has come that on the Ides of March a group of senators murdered Julius Caesar.
news.n_cicero: News has come that the orator Cicero has been killed on the orders of Rome's new masters.
news.n_philippi: News has come that at Philippi Antony and Octavian defeated Caesar's murderers. Brutus and Cassius took their own lives.
news.n_herod: News has come that, with Roman help, Herod has taken Jerusalem and become king of Judea.
news.n_zhizhi: Far to the east, they say, a Han army marched to the far western steppes and destroyed a rebel Xiongnu chief at his timber fort.
news.n_zhaojun: Merchants from the East say the Han emperor has given a lady of his court, Wang Zhaojun, in marriage to a nomad chief. Songs are already being sung of her beauty.
news.n_actium: News has come that at Actium Octavian has defeated the fleet of Antony and Cleopatra. They have fled to Egypt.
news.n_cleopatra: News has come that Antony and Cleopatra have taken their own lives. Egypt has become a possession of Rome.
news.n_augustus: News has come that the Senate has granted Octavian the name Augustus. He says he has restored the Republic, but everyone knows who rules now.
news.n_aelius_gallus: Merchants from the Red Sea say a Roman army marched into Arabia Felix in search of incense, but desert and disease destroyed it.
news.n_kush: They say an army of Kushites from beyond the cataracts of the Nile attacked Syene, and the Romans struck back as far as their capital, Napata.
news.n_vitruvius: They say the architect Vitruvius has dedicated ten books on architecture to Augustus: on buildings that are strong, useful and beautiful.
news.n_parthian_standards: News has come that the Parthians have handed back, without a fight, the standards taken from Crassus. Rome is jubilant.
news.n_herod_temple: They say King Herod has begun rebuilding the Temple in Jerusalem with unheard-of splendour.
news.n_virgil: News has come that the poet Virgil has died. He asked for his unfinished "Aeneid" to be burned, but Augustus forbade it.
news.n_drusus: They say Drusus, Augustus' stepson, led his army as far as the Elbe in Germania but fell from his horse on the way back and died.
news.n_herod_death: News has come that King Herod has died. His kingdom has been divided among his sons.
news.n_han_census: Merchants from the East tell an incredible tale: the land of silk has counted all its people, and found nearly sixty million.
news.n_judea_province: News has come that Judea has become a Roman province. Quirinius, governor of Syria, is holding a census there.
news.n_teutoburg: Terrible news has come: in the Teutoburg Forest the Germans destroyed the three legions of Varus. They say Augustus cries out at night, "Varus, give me back my legions!"
news.n_wang_mang: Far to the east, in the land of silk, the minister Wang Mang has deposed the Han dynasty and proclaimed himself emperor of a new one.
news.n_augustus_death: News has come that Augustus has died after ruling for more than forty years. His stepson Tiberius is emperor.
news.n_ovid: Merchants from the Black Sea say the poet Ovid has died in exile at Tomis, at the edge of the empire.
news.n_germanicus: News has come that Germanicus, the people's favourite, has died suddenly at Antioch. Many suspect poison.
news.n_sacrovir: They say debtors in Gaul rose up under Florus and Sacrovir, but the legions quickly put down the revolt.
news.n_han_restored: Far to the east, they say, after turmoil and famine a kinsman of the old emperors has restored the Han dynasty, with a new capital at Luoyang.
news.n_jesus: In Judea, the Roman governor Pontius Pilate executed a preacher named Jesus of Nazareth. Few noticed at the time.
news.n_tiberius_death: News has come that the old emperor Tiberius has died. The new emperor is young Gaius, whom the soldiers call Caligula.
news.n_mauretania: They say Caligula summoned King Ptolemy of Mauretania to Rome and had him executed. The lands beyond Carthage are becoming Roman.
news.n_caligula_killed: News has come that the Praetorians have killed Caligula. His uncle Claudius has been proclaimed emperor.
news.n_britain_conquest: News has come that Claudius' legions have landed in Britain. They say the emperor came there himself, with elephants.
news.n_aksum: Merchants from the Red Sea tell of the port of Adulis and of the city of the Aksumites in the mountains beyond, where ivory comes from.
news.n_boudica: News has come that in Britain Queen Boudica has risen up and burned Londinium, but the Romans have crushed her army.
news.n_pompeii_quake: They say a strong earthquake has damaged much of Pompeii and Herculaneum at the foot of Vesuvius. People are rebuilding.
news.n_seneca: News has come that after a plot against Nero was uncovered, the philosopher Seneca was ordered to die, and he opened his veins.
news.n_jewish_revolt: News has come that a revolt against Rome has broken out in Judea. The Roman garrison in Jerusalem has been wiped out.
news.n_tiridates: They say the Parthian prince Tiridates has come to Rome, and Nero placed the crown of Armenia on his head with his own hands.
news.n_nero_olympia: From the Olympic Games comes the story that Emperor Nero won the chariot race, though he fell out of his chariot and never finished.
news.n_white_horse: Merchants from the East say that in the land of silk, at Luoyang, the first temple of the Buddha's teaching has been built: the White Horse Monastery.
news.n_four_emperors: News has come that since Nero's death four emperors have followed one another in a single year. The general Vespasian has come out on top.
news.n_jerusalem_70: News has come that Titus, son of Vespasian, has taken Jerusalem. The Temple has been burned and destroyed.
news.n_masada: They say the last fortress of the Judean rebels, Masada on its rock above the Dead Sea, has fallen.
news.n_pliny_nh: They say Pliny the Elder has dedicated his "Natural History" to the emperor: a vast work about everything in the world, from stars to stones.
news.n_vesuvius: News has come that Vesuvius has erupted and buried Pompeii and Herculaneum in ash. Pliny the Elder died too, trying to rescue people.
news.n_colosseum: They say a vast amphitheatre of the Flavians has opened in Rome, and the opening games lasted a hundred days.
news.n_mons_graupius: They say the general Agricola has reached the far north of Britain and defeated the Caledonians at Mons Graupius.
news.n_ikh_bayan: Far to the east, they say, a Han army has finally crushed the northern Xiongnu. The nomads are moving west.
news.n_domitian: News has come that Emperor Domitian has been murdered in his own palace. The Senate has chosen old Nerva as emperor.
news.n_gan_ying: Merchants from the East say an envoy of the land of silk set out to reach Rome but got only as far as a western sea: sailors scared him off with tales of a long and dangerous voyage.
news.n_trajan: News has come that Trajan is emperor, the first from Spain rather than Italy. And the historian Tacitus has written a book about the Germans.
news.n_dacian_war: News has come that Trajan has gone to war against the Dacians beyond the Danube and their king Decebalus.
news.n_paper: Merchants from the East say that in the land of silk a courtier named Cai Lun has learned to make writing material from bark, rags and old nets, cheap and light.
news.n_dacia_province: News has come that Dacia is conquered and Decebalus is dead. They say Dacian gold is pouring into Rome like a river.
news.n_arabia_province: Merchants from the East say the kingdom of the Nabataeans and its city of Petra have become part of the empire as the province of Arabia.
news.n_trajan_column: They say Trajan's Column has been set up in Rome, with the whole story of the Dacian war winding round it in a spiral.
news.n_antioch_quake: News has come that a terrible earthquake has wrecked Antioch, where Emperor Trajan was wintering. He himself survived.
news.n_persian_gulf: They say Trajan has taken the Parthian capital Ctesiphon and marched all the way to the Persian Gulf.
news.n_hadrian: News has come that Trajan has died on his way back from the East. Hadrian is emperor and has at once given up the new conquests.
news.n_hadrian_wall: They say Hadrian has ordered a wall built right across Britain, from sea to sea, to shut out the northern tribes.
news.n_pantheon: They say the Pantheon in Rome has been rebuilt with an enormous dome and a round opening to the sky.
news.n_kanishka: Merchants from the East say a mighty Kushan king named Kanishka rules the lands between India and the steppe.
news.n_seismoscope: Far to the east, they say, a scholar named Zhang Heng has built a bronze vessel with dragons that shows by itself in which direction a distant earthquake struck.
news.n_bar_kokhba: News has come that the Bar Kokhba revolt in Judea has been crushed. A Roman city is being built on the site of Jerusalem, and Jews are forbidden to enter it.
news.n_hadrian_death: News has come that Emperor Hadrian has died. Antoninus is the new emperor.
news.n_antonine_wall: They say the Romans in Britain have pushed further north and are building a new rampart of turf there.
news.n_rome_900: They say Rome is celebrating the nine-hundredth anniversary of its founding in grand style.
news.n_almagest: They say the Alexandrian astronomer Ptolemy has written a great book on the motions of the Sun, Moon and planets around the Earth.
news.n_galen_gladiators: They say that in Pergamon a young doctor named Galen is treating gladiators, and hardly any of his patients have died.
news.n_marcus: News has come that Emperor Antoninus Pius has died. Now two men rule together: Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus.
news.n_galen_rome: They say the doctor Galen of Pergamon has come to Rome and dissects animals in public to show how the body works.
news.n_seleucia: News has come that a Roman army in the East has taken the Parthian cities of Seleucia and Ctesiphon.
news.n_envoy_han: They say men calling themselves envoys of the Roman emperor have reached the court of the emperor of the land of silk by sea.
news.n_aquileia: Alarming news has come: the Germanic Marcomanni and Quadi have crossed the Danube and besieged Aquileia. Barbarians are in Italy for the first time since the Cimbri.
news.n_avidius: News has come that the general Avidius Cassius in the East, believing a false rumour of Marcus Aurelius' death, proclaimed himself emperor, and was soon killed by his own men.
news.n_stone_classics: Far to the east, they say, at Luoyang the texts of the ancient classics are being carved on stone tablets so that no one can corrupt them in copying.
news.n_athens_chairs: They say Marcus Aurelius has established salaried chairs in Athens for teachers of all four schools of philosophy.
news.n_marcus_death: News has come that the philosopher-emperor Marcus Aurelius has died in an army camp on the Danube. His son Commodus is emperor.
news.n_yellow_turbans: Merchants from the East say a huge rebellion of peasants wearing yellow headbands has broken out in the land of silk.
news.n_luoyang_burned: Far to the east, they say, the warlord Dong Zhuo has burned the capital Luoyang and carried the emperor off to the west.
news.n_commodus: News has come that on the last day of the year Emperor Commodus, who used to fight in the arena as a gladiator, has been murdered.
news.n_severus: News has come that five men have claimed the throne in a single year, and the Praetorians even auctioned it off. Septimius Severus from Africa has won.
news.n_byzantium: Word in the harbour is that after a long siege Severus has taken Byzantium and torn down its walls.
news.n_lugdunum: News has come that near Lugdunum in Gaul Severus has defeated his last rival, Clodius Albinus.
news.n_guandu: Far to the east, they say, the warlord Cao Cao defeated a much larger rival army at Guandu and became master of the north of the land of silk.
